report.summary: Chunk 2 of 5 of daedalus/mapping/reach.py: dataclass _Src, path walking, main-guard detection, branch literal extraction, dispatch chain detection, dead-branch/import-error handling, import splitting, module-level bindings, shim detection.

handoff.purpose: Source scanning utilities: _Src scratch, file walking, main-guard, branch literals, dispatch chains, dead-branch/import-error handling, import splitting, module-level bindings, shim detection.

symbols.name: _Src
symbols.note: Mutable scratch for one parsed module; fields for records, function-scoped records, names, calls, loops, dispatch, main-guard flag, shim flag, literals, dynamic, weak imports, toplevel names.

symbols.name: _py_dotted
symbols.note: Converts a relative .py path to dotted module name: strips last 3 chars and replaces '/' with '.'.

symbols.name: _iter_py
symbols.note: Walks a root Path, yields sorted list of relative .py paths.

symbols.name: _walk
symbols.note: Wrapper around os.walk that sorts dirnames and filenames, filters out _IGNORE_DIRS and dot-directories.

symbols.name: _is_main_guard
symbols.note: Returns True if node is an ast.If with test `__name__ == '__main__'` (single comparison, constant string).

symbols.name: _branch_literals
symbols.note: Extracts string literals from a branch condition: from Compare (left and comparators), BoolOp recursively, and Call to str.startswith/endswith.

symbols.name: _dispatch_chains
symbols.note: Finds flat if/elif chains inside a function, returns list of chains of (literal, node) pairs, only chains with at least _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES.

symbols.name: _IMPORT_ERRORS
symbols.note: Tuple of import error names: ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError.

symbols.name: _is_never_true
symbols.note: Returns True for `if False:` / `if 0:` — ast.Constant that is falsy.

symbols.name: _catches_import_error
symbols.note: Returns True if a try node has a handler that names ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError (or attribute thereof).

symbols.name: _split_imports
symbols.note: Returns (live, weak) import records for a subtree, with context-sensitive handling of dead branches and suppressed ImportError.

symbols.name: _import_records_of
symbols.note: Returns only live import records from a node.

symbols.name: _toplevel_names
symbols.note: Returns set of names bound at module import time, descending into if/try/with up to depth 3.

symbols.name: _module_level_bindings
symbols.note: Maps module-level import-bound names to import records.

symbols.name: _shim_body
symbols.note: Returns True if module body re-exports and does nothing else; structural detection.

claims.text: A branch we cannot read contributes nothing rather than a guess.
claims.why: The function only appends literals when it recognizes specific AST shapes (Compare, BoolOp, Call with startswith/endswith); unrecognized shapes yield no literals.

claims.text: Covers the two shapes real dispatch chains use: `x == "literal"` and `x.startswith("/api/")`
claims.why: The function handles Compare (which includes x == literal) and Call with startswith/endswith attributes.

claims.text: A chain is only a command table when it is long enough (`_MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES`); shorter ones are ordinary conditionals and reporting them as subcommands would fabricate entry points.
claims.why: The function only appends a chain to the result if len(chain) >= _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES.

claims.text: `if False:` / `if 0:` -- a branch the interpreter deletes. Deliberately literal-only. Inferring that some NAME is falsy would make the walk guess, and a guess in this direction silently deletes real edges.
claims.why: The function returns True only for ast.Constant with falsy value; it does not handle Name or other expressions.

claims.text: Only handlers that NAME ImportError (or ModuleNotFoundError) count. A bare `except Exception` around an import is usually a lazy-optional-dependency idiom too, but widening this rule reclassifies real edges on evidence that is not there.
claims.why: The function only returns True if handler type is a Name or Attribute whose id/attr is in _IMPORT_ERRORS; bare except Exception (type None) is skipped.

claims.text: Structural descent rather than `ast.walk` because the whole point is the CONTEXT an import sits in: the same statement is evidence in one branch and not in another.
claims.why: The implementation uses a recursive rec() that descends via ast.iter_child_nodes, with special handling for If (dead branch) and Try (suppressed import), which ast.walk would not provide.

claims.text: The else IS the live branch
claims.why: In the dead-branch case, the orelse is recursively processed with the same 'why', making it live.

claims.text: the handler's own import is the fallback that actually runs
claims.why: The handler body is recursively processed with the original 'why' (empty if no prior suppression), so those imports become live.

claims.text: LIVE import records only. Weak ones are reachable only via :func:`_split_imports`, so no caller can pick them up by accident.
claims.why: The function returns only the first element of _split_imports, which is the live list.

claims.text: Names a module binds at import time. Descends one level into `if` and `try` because conditional definitions are ordinary in this codebase.
claims.why: The function collects names from FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef, ClassDef, Assign, AnnAssign, AugAssign, Import, ImportFrom, and recurses into If, Try, With, AsyncWith with depth limit 3.

claims.text: MODULE LEVEL ONLY, and that restriction is load-bearing. ... Binding names from every scope made `m` resolve to all sixty modules, so every subcommand appeared to reach every other subcommand's target and the whole dispatch collapsed into one blob. A branch's own imports are handled separately, from that branch's own records.
claims.why: The function iterates only over tree.body (module-level statements), not nested scopes. Branch-level imports are handled elsewhere (presumably by _split_imports).

claims.text: Detected structurally, never guessed: no def, no class, no executable statement beyond imports, `__all__` and plain alias assignments.
claims.why: The function body shown is incomplete; it only shows the start of the loop, not the full logic that checks for defs, classes, or executable statements beyond imports. The claim extends beyond the visible code.

claims.text: A shim is worth naming because it is the one module class where "nothing reaches it" is expected rather than alarming.
claims.why: This is a rationale comment, not a checkable behavioral claim within this chunk.

observations.what: _walk uses os.walk directly, not the imported os module at top; it imports os locally inside the function.
_iter_py sorts the resulting list, while _walk already sorts filenames; double sorting is redundant but harmless.
_is_main_guard only handles `__name__ == '__main__'` with a single comparison; it does not handle other forms like `__name__ != '__main__'` or reversed operands.
_branch_literals handles `startswith`/`endswith` but not `in` or regex patterns; it may miss some dispatch conditions.
_split_imports treats the handler body as live even if the try has no ImportError suppression; it only applies the suppression to the try body and orelse, not the handler body.
_toplevel_names has a depth limit of 3; deeper nested conditional definitions may be missed.
